title: AFP/PIVKA-II double-positive status indicates a high-risk subtype of hepatocellular carcinoma in liver transplantation: retrospective cohort study and phosphoproteome evaluation
message.abstract:
<jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Introduction:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>Liver transplantation (LT) is one of the therapeutic options for hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). α-fetoprotein (AFP) and protein induced by vitamin K absence or antagonist II (PIVKA-II) serologic levels are commonly used in monitoring HCC and have been reported to correlate with LT prognosis. This study aimed to evaluate the overall survival (OS) and tumor-free survival (TFS) after LT in HCC recipients with different preoperative AFP and PIVKA-II status, and to profile HCC molecular characteristics based on phosphoproteome.</jats:p>
                  </jats:sec>
                  <jats:sec>
                    <jats:title>Methods:</jats:title>
                    <jats:p>HCC patients undergoing LT from 2015 to 2022 were identified in a clinical multicenter database of the Chinese Liver Transplant Registry. HCC recipients with different AFP and PIVKA-II statuses (A+P+, A−P−, A+P−, A−P+) were compared after propensity score matching.
